overview: Black meets 1.g3 with a Dutch-style ...f5, taking e4 under control and claiming kingside space. White normally plays 2.Bg2 Nf6 3.Nf3 and the game transposes to a Dutch against a fianchetto set-up, with Black choosing between a Stonewall (...e6, ...d5), a Leningrad (...g6, ...d6) or a Classical ...e6/...d6 formation. White presses on the long diagonal and the e4 break; Black plays for kingside space and the e4 square. Play is strategic and slow rather than forcing, but ...f5 leaves the king and e6 square a little loose.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto Bg2, Nf3, O-O and aim the bishop at b7/e4 square
Prepare d4/c4 and a later e4 or Nh4 break to challenge f5
Exploit the weakened e6 and the long diagonal once Black commits to ...e6

black_ideas.idea: Control e4 with ...f5 and ...Nf6, then build a Stonewall with ...e6, ...d5, ...c6
Leningrad set-up with ...g6, ...Bg7, ...d6 and ...e5 for central space
Kingside expansion with ...Ne4 outpost or ...g5 later

typical_structures.structure: Stonewall: Black pawns on c6, d5, e6, f5 against White's g3/d3 or d4 set-up
Leningrad Dutch: Black pawns d6/f5 with ...e5 break against a g3 fianchetto

character.notes: White's 1.g3 and 2.Bg2 keep things slow, so this is quieter than the main-line Dutch, but ...f5 still weakens the king and the e6/e8-h5 diagonal. Not forcing early; I read it as Balanced and it could be called Sharp by analogy with the Dutch.

soundness.notes: The Dutch against a g3 fianchetto is entirely sound; White gets at most a small edge.

structure.notes: Centre not yet decided: Black may go Stonewall (closed) or Leningrad ...e5 (tension). Flexible.

approach.notes: A recognised Dutch reply to a flank opening, played at all levels. Standard.

level.notes: Dutch set-ups need a feel for where the king and e4 square are weak; little forced theory against 1.g3. Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: Stonewall set-up
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. g3 f5 2. Bg2 Nf6 3. Nf3 e6 4. O-O Be7 5. d3 O-O 6. c4 d5
sublines_that_differ.how: Locks the centre and gives Black a closed, kingside-minded structure.

sublines_that_differ.name: Leningrad set-up
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. g3 f5 2. Bg2 Nf6 3. Nf3 g6 4. O-O Bg7 5. d3 d6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black aims for ...e5 with a more dynamic centre.

character.reason: A Dutch reply to a slow fianchetto: no early forcing play, but ...f5 weakens Black's king.

soundness.reason: The Dutch against 1.g3 is a normal, healthy reply.

structure.reason: Black can choose a Stonewall or a Leningrad ...e5 set-up, so the centre is undecided.

approach.reason: A respectable reply to 1.g3 used at all levels, not a set-up to play against everything.

level.reason: Little to memorise but Dutch king safety and e4 control need judgement.

plans.reason: Both sides usually fianchetto a bishop; no other plan is clearly dominant.
